## Slide 1

Kestrel Arts Alliance — Studio Pathways Logic Model INPUTS Staffing: One studio manager and three teaching artists on contract Staffing: A part-time administrator covering intake and scheduling Facilities: A ceramics studio and a shared darkroom on Kestrel Street Funding: A three-year city arts grant renewed each April ACTIVITIES Instruction: Twelve-week studio courses in ceramics and photography Instruction: Open studio hours four afternoons a week Outreach: Portfolio review clinics for applying secondary students Outreach: An annual exhibition of participant work at the city library OUTPUTS Participation: Ninety young people completing at least one studio course Participation: Six hundred open studio visits logged across the year Product: Forty finished portfolios assembled and reviewed SHORT-TERM OUTCOMES Skills: Participants demonstrate competent use of studio equipment Confidence: Participants describe themselves as artists to their peers LONG-TERM OUTCOMES Pathways: Participants apply to arts programmes after secondary school Community: Kestrel Street sustains a visible community of young makers
